memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then Moses and Aaron were brought back to Pharaoh. "Go, worship the Lord your God," he said. "But tell me who will be going." Moses answered, "We will go with our young and our old, with our sons and our daughters, and with our flocks and herds, because we are to celebrate a festival to the Lord."" - Exodus 10:8-9 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Pharaoh finally says go — and then immediately asks a narrowing question: tell me who will be going.

Moses' answer is magnificent in its completeness. Young and old. Sons and daughters. Flocks and herds. Everyone and everything. No one left behind.

That is the right instinct about worship. It is not a specialist activity for the spiritually gifted or the free-time-rich. It includes the toddler and the grandmother, the ones who understand and the ones who are still learning.

We often unconsciously divide our households — some members are "the religious ones" while others are excused. Joshua refused that split: as for me and my household, we will serve the Lord (Josh 24:15).

And notice that even the livestock go. Worship involves our work and our possessions, not just our souls. Nothing is exempt.

If you are the only believer in your home, this is a picture to pray toward. God's heart is for whole households.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I quietly excused certain people or areas of life from worship?
2. What would it look like for my whole household to serve God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, I want all of my life and all of my household to belong to You. Draw everyone in my home to Yourself. Amen.
